subject: Archaeology
title: Neanderthal DNA in Modern Humans
description: Learn Neanderthal DNA in Modern Humans in one minute.

hook.text: If you have European or Asian ancestry, about two percent of your DNA is Neanderthal.

buildup.text: Svante Pääbo sequenced the Neanderthal genome in 2010, proving interbreeding with humans.

discovery.text: Neanderthal DNA influences skin color, immune response, and sleep patterns today.

twist.text: Some inherited genes helped survival. Others are linked to autoimmune diseases.

climax.text: Pääbo won the 2022 Nobel Prize for founding paleogenomics — reading DNA of the dead.

punchline.text: Neanderthals vanished 40,000 years ago. Their DNA still shapes your body.

quiz.question: What did Svante Pääbo's Nobel-winning work reveal?
options: Neanderthals were a subspecies of humans, not separate
People of European and Asian descent carry about 2% Neanderthal DNA
Neanderthals went extinct due to a single global pandemic

details.summary: Modern non-African humans carry roughly 1-4% Neanderthal DNA, proving that Homo sapiens and Neanderthals interbred when they coexisted in Europe and western Asia. This ancient DNA influences modern human traits including immune response, skin pigmentation, and disease susceptibility.
details.whyItMatters: The discovery that humans carry Neanderthal DNA demolished the idea that Homo sapiens replaced all other human species without interaction. It reveals a complex history of coexistence and interbreeding.
takeaways: Non-African humans carry 1-4% Neanderthal DNA from interbreeding
Inherited genes affect immunity, skin, and disease susceptibility
This proves Homo sapiens and Neanderthals coexisted and interbred

faq.question: How do scientists extract DNA from Neanderthal bones?
faq.answer: DNA survives in cool, dry conditions for tens of thousands of years. Scientists drill small samples from bones, extract surviving DNA fragments, and use sequencing technology to reconstruct genomes. Svante Pääbo's team pioneered these methods, winning the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physiology.

faq.question: What modern traits come from Neanderthal DNA?
faq.answer: Neanderthal genes influence immune system responses to pathogens, skin and hair characteristics adapted to northern climates, and even susceptibility to conditions like depression and blood clotting disorders. Some Neanderthal immune genes actually provided advantages against local diseases.
